## The decision

**The operator has adopted option (a) of bug `f850-674c-c89f-4b97` (`unsuited-locustal-incatern`):
Windows IS now a declared support target for rebar.**

That converts `sweep (windows)` from "a permanently-red job that is not a health signal" into a
**known-incomplete support target being driven to green**. The job has never passed since
`7024c35790bc` added it (2026-08-26): no onset boundary, nothing regressed — the sweep simply
revealed that rebar does not run on Windows. The decision and the obligations it creates are
recorded in **ADR 0117** (`docs/adr/0117-windows-declared-support-target.md`), landed by task
`arterial-bilineate-vampirebat` (`a01e-01e7-6e6e-4809`); this epic is the execution vehicle.

## Scope, from measured evidence

Source: job `100874330553` of run `33824556786`, final line
`510 failed, 5140 passed, 69 skipped, 206 warnings, 74 errors in 662.75s`. The log was re-read for
this decomposition rather than trusted from the bug's summary: 584 `FAILED`/`ERROR` lines across
**110 distinct test files**. Counts below are `E ` lines, so they over/under-count individual tests
slightly — they are for ORDERING, not a burn-down target.

| Class | Evidence | Child |
|---|---|---|
| `fcntl` unguarded use in `_store/lock.py` | 384 `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flock'` + 4 `ModuleNotFoundError: 'fcntl'` | S1 — **gates everything** |
| Network guard leaks on Windows | 47 `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests` | S2 |
| POSIX mode-bit / permission assertions | 17 `CleanupError: artifact directory must not be group/world accessible`, plus `st_mode`/`chmod` sites | S3 |
| Path-separator string semantics | 217 backslashed-path occurrences, e.g. `assert 'src/rebar/live.py:1' in '…src\rebar\live.py:1…'` | S4 |
| `os.path.relpath` across drive letters | 2 `ValueError: path is on mount 'C:', start on mount 'D:'` | S5 |
| CRLF newline translation | `assert b'{\r\n  "bin…' == b'{\n  "bindi…'` | S6 |
| cp1252 / charmap console codec | 5 `UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x8f`, 2 `'utf-8' … 0x97` | S7 |
| Windows mandatory locking on unlink/rename | 7 `PermissionError [WinError 32]` / `[WinError 5]` | S8 |
| POSIX exec and signal semantics | 3 `OSError [WinError 193] %1 is not a valid Win32 application`; a signal kill surfaced as a POSITIVE returncode; `.sh`-dependent gate tests | S9 |

## The ordering is not negotiable — `lock.py` FIRST

`src/rebar/_store/lock.py` is roughly **74% of the failures on its own** and gates every other
class: every store write reaches `_acquire_once` → `_acquire_fcntl` (`lock.py:491`), so on Windows
every ticket write raises `AttributeError`. Until that is fixed the other classes cannot even be
measured — their tests fail on store setup before reaching the semantics under test.

The bug's ".EXE console-script invocation" class is downstream of S1: those `CalledProcessError`s
carry the `flock` `AttributeError` as stderr. Class sizes above are estimates until S1 is green.

**S1 therefore `blocks` every other child.** Do not work S2–S9 in parallel with S1.

`lock.py` is not the only site. FULL census of `fcntl` users in `src/rebar`
(`grep -rl fcntl src/rebar --include='*.py'`, each hit read), with disposition:

* **S1** — `_store/lock.py` (`:207`, `:254`) and `_commands/doctor_locks.py` (`:142`, `:148`):
  guarded import, unguarded use, both probing the same `.ticket-write.lock`.
* **`discrete-unrelative-vervet` (`a50a-cac1-af18-42d9`)** — `reducer/marker.py` (`:33`, `:37`):
  same shape, different lock (the `.archived` marker).
* **`hyperbolic-humanoid-owl` (`658e-a99b-a004-4be3`)** — `_store/fsutil.py:82`: a function-local
  `import fcntl` ⇒ `ModuleNotFoundError` at CALL time, on the HLC-stamp write path
  (`_store/hlc.py:94`); these are the 4 `ModuleNotFoundError` lines above. It is a BLOCKING
  acquire, so it needs a blocking take S1's selector does not expose; `depends_on` S1.
* **Already correct, no work** — `llm/gate_admission.py` (its entry point early-returns at `:319`
  on `fcntl is None`, so `:233`/`:259` are unreachable); `_store/git_locking.py`,
  `_snapshot/git_fetch.py`, `_snapshot/janitor.py`, `rebar_reconciler/alert_store.py` (import AND
  use guarded); `_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` (guarded import, no `flock` call).
* **No symbol use** — every other hit is a docstring/comment mention.

`scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py` passed the bad files because it checks only the import
(`greisen-enjoyable-zethuswasp`, `bf74-a636-e6d9-40f9`); a runtime-use gate is the natural
follow-on. Anything this census misses is caught by AC2's `0 failed, 0 errors`.

## Do NOT flip `sweep (windows)` to gating on day one

Making the job voting now would redden **every** change with 510 unrelated failures — wrecking the
`Verified` signal, the precise failure mode ADR 0114 exists to prevent. The flip is the **last**
child (S11) and is the criterion that proves this epic done. Until then the job stays
`continue-on-error: true`, but its meaning changes from "ignorable" to "tracked and being driven to
green" — which is what S10 makes visible in the tree.

Per **ADR 0114** the flip is itself two steps: the job must show one passing `main` run outside the
required `Verified` hot path before a separate change promotes it into the aggregate in
`.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.

S11 must also **re-measure the Windows lane on a green run**: in run `33824556786` it took 11m47s
against `sweep (macos, full suite)`'s 52m38s, so Windows is not the expensive lane, and 662.75s is
a floor measured where 510 tests failed early.

## The comment in `test.yml` is now FALSE

`.github/workflows/test.yml:329-333` reads:

> Non-blocking: Windows is not yet a declared support target, so a genuine incompatibility is a
> visible finding, never a red gate.

Under this decision that sentence is untrue. **S10** corrects it: unblocked, costs nothing, and
stops the tree asserting the opposite of the decision while the epic runs.

A single-line `grep` for it is **vacuous** — it wraps across two physical comment lines, so the
joined phrase matches nothing even on the uncorrected tree. Any check must join the lines and
normalise whitespace first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every child S1–S9 is closed with its own named proving command passing on `windows-latest`.
      Proof: each child's recorded proving command, run on a `windows-latest` job.
- [ ] `sweep (windows)` reports `0 failed, 0 errors` on a scheduled or dispatched run of `main`.
      Proof (deterministic even while the job is `continue-on-error`, where `gh run watch
      --exit-status` would exit 0 regardless): `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main`, then
      `gh run view <id> --log --job "sweep (windows)" | tail -1` must match
      `^[0-9]+ passed` with no `failed`/`error` term — equivalently
      `... | grep -cE '[0-9]+ (failed|error)'` prints `0`.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/test.yml` contains no statement that Windows is not a support target.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_windows_support_target.py`, which joins and whitespace-
      normalises the comment lines rather than grepping a single line.
- [ ] `sweep (windows)` (or its successor) is in the `Verified` aggregate, promoted per ADR 0114
      with the prior independent green `main` run cited in the promotion change. Proof: the job
      appears in `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s blocking `needs` and the change cites that run id.
- [ ] No child weakens the `fcntl_held=True` precondition in `_acquire_mkdir` (`lock.py:325-362`)
      without replacing the exclusivity proof it depends on, and a test fails if that invariant is
      degraded (AC5 of `f850-674c-c89f-4b97`, carried forward). Proof: a named test that fails
      when the precondition is degraded, cited on S1.

## Proving command for the epic as a whole

```
gh workflow run test.yml --ref main
gh run view <id> --log --job "sweep (windows)" | grep -cE '[0-9]+ (failed|error)'  # must be 0
```
